content.text:
The drawing shows a 3,5-dinitrothiophene joined through an azo group to a substituted benzene.

**Thiophene ring.** The sulfur is at the bottom. C2 is attached to the azo group. C3 carries NO2 at the top. C4 is a CH. C5 carries NO2 at the lower left and is bonded to S. The double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5.

**Azo linker.** N=N connects thiophene C2 to the benzene ring.

**Benzene ring.** The carbon bearing the azo group (call it C1) is at the left. Going around the ring from C1:
- The lower-left neighbour carries a methyl group (the methyl points down).
- The next ring carbon is CH.
- Then comes the carbon bearing N(Et)2, at the right.
- The two remaining carbons are CH.

So the methyl is ortho to the azo group and the diethylamino group is para to it.

SMILES for the thiophene part: [O-][N+](=O)c1cc([N+](=O)[O-])c(s1)N=N...

Full SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(N=Nc2sc([N+](=O)[O-])cc2[N+](=O)[O-])c(C)c1

Check of the benzene ring: c1 (NEt2), c, c, c(N=N), c(C), c1 closing back to the NEt2 carbon. The azo carbon is para to NEt2, the methyl carbon is adjacent to the azo carbon, and the ring closes through a CH. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(N=Nc2sc([N+](=O)[O-])cc2[N+](=O)[O-])c(C)c1
